headline: Classic characters that shaped modern superhero media
post:
Long before caped crusaders dominated pop culture, iconic pulp heroes, radio stars, and newspaper comic strip icons paved the way for our favorite champions. According to Screen Rant, classic figures like Zorro helped popularize the brilliant "dual identity" trope that later defined heroes like Batman and Superman. Meanwhile, legendary pulp crime fighters like The Shadow introduced dark, atmospheric storytelling that heavily influenced the genre.

From the skin-tight suit of The Phantom to the groundbreaking sidekick dynamic of The Green Hornet, these early adventurers laid the crucial groundwork for modern comic books. Even characters without actual powers, like Dick Tracy, left a massive mark by establishing colorful rogues' galleries filled with gimmick-driven villains.

Which of these classic pulp and comic strip heroes is your all-time favorite? 🦸‍♂️

#Superheroes #ComicHistory #PopCulture
original_title: 10 Characters Who Inspired Modern Superhero Media

headline: Absolute Firestorm's Monstrous New Look Revealed
post:

headline: Remembering Stacy Keach and Mask of the Phantasm
post:
Actor Stacy Keach reportedly passed away on November 10, 2026, leaving behind a remarkable legacy across film, television, and theatre. DC Comics and Batman fans will fondly remember his memorable voice work in Batman: Mask of the Phantasm, where he played both Carl Beaumont and the haunting voice of the Phantasm.

Keach brought a deep and ghostly presence to the role in the beloved animated film, alongside Kevin Conroy's iconic performance as Batman. Our thoughts are with his loved ones during this time.

Further updates will be provided as they become available.

#StacyKeach #Batman #MaskOfThePhantasm
original_title: Stacy Keach Played A Villain In One Of The Best Batman Movies Of All Time
